slices.name: ws01-26-status-buttons-chips-scrollpanel
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 26 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD a74f221 (slice 25); the base for diffs is a74f221. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, lines 7 to 11; the acceptance table with its AC5 row (line 29), its AC14 row (line 38), its AC8 row (line 32, which still says the fixture's badges draw fixed colours), its AC13 row (line 37, step 31's) and its T2 row (line 58, the pattern for a filled row); the step 25 block (lines 653 to 686) and the step 24 block (lines 620 to 651); Decisions (Tokens from step 21, line 743; Status colours, A printed page takes the light look, Browsers that cannot mix colours and Light islands from step 24, lines 752 to 755; Gold text and Ground-aware colour moves from step 25, lines 756 and 757); Deviations (ScrollPanel (step 26), line 873; Step 24, line 985; Step 25, line 995); Verify items (Light tones on navy and StatusBadge from step 24, lines 1139 and 1140; The dark spot run (step 24), 1147; StatusBadge (step 25), 1162); Follow-ups (the step 24 ones that step 25 closed: Gold hex text is step 25's, every use of it, line 1287, and the gold part of Dark mode on pages not converted yet, line 1259; the ones it left to this slice: StatusBadge's tones, 1288, the StatusBadge part of line 1259, Tokens with no reader yet, 1263, Muted StatusBadge contrast (step 20), 1255, and Selected navy controls in dark mode, 1274, which names FilterChip; and Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS, 1273, Gold grounds in dark mode, 1275, and What the gold guard's reading leaves out (step 25), 1302, whose last sentence says this slice keeps StatusBadge's light gold entry true or takes it out), and steps 20 to 25), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (the tile rule at line 289, the WS01 components at lines 303 to 306, the static live dot at 313, the new files at 335 and 336, acceptance criteria 5 and 14 at lines 352 and 361, the planned tests at 365 and 369, the WS01 deviations list at line 112, and WS04's note at line 119 that FilterChips.tsx becomes FilterBar.tsx), the boards the shapes come from (the manifest entry names none, only K's October 8 note): docs/redesign/lca-redesign-boards/boards/Looks-3-Minimal-Tile.dc.html (status tags, the gold button and the quick-filter chips; its .t-tag and .t-chip rules), docs/redesign/decided-boards/Tourn-Table-Final.dc.html (the active filter chip with its button labelled Remove filter: Next 3 months), Event-Final-Setup.dc.html (note 13: the setup form scrolls in its own container while the steps rail and the page preview stay in view) and Event-Final-States.dc.html (the Event full wording), src/components/StatusBadge.tsx (all 99 lines), src/components/ui/button.tsx and badge.tsx, src/lib/brand.ts, src/lib/features.ts, src/areas/events/tournamentStatus.ts, src/index.css (the utilities at lines 72 to 87; the plain :root status tokens at 252 to 267; the status tokens of the new look in the base block at 417 to 432, dark at 473 to 488, live at 526 to 541 and scholastic at 578 to 593, with heritage restyling none; the tones at 643 to 687; the focus ring at 724 to 757; the motion rule at 759 to 771; the block for browsers that cannot mix colours at 786 to 808), src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx, src/pages/ScholasticPage.tsx, TournamentsPage.tsx, HomePage.tsx, NewsPage.tsx (line 145) and src/components/layout/Footer.tsx (line 115) for the way a visible word is shown under newLook only, test/unit/news-pinned.test.tsx and news-pinned-off.test.tsx and appearance-control.test.tsx with appearance-control-off.test.tsx for the pair of tests that mock src/lib/features, domain/format/date.ts (formatDate at line 136, zonedParts at line 82) with domain/format/index.ts and src/lib/format.ts, the tests that pin StatusBadge today: test/unit/render-smoke.test.tsx (lines 18 to 35), tokens.test.ts (lines 122 to 135), contrast.test.ts (lines 655 to 717 and 906), goldText.test.ts (lines 742, 794 to 798, 1075 and 1165), fixtures/goldAllowlist.ts (entries at lines 51 and 112), raw-colours.test.ts (lines 164, 198 to 200, 307, 339 to 346 and 446), fixtures/raw-colours-allowlist.json (lines 17 and 36 to 43), semantic-map.test.ts (lines 783 to 822), dark-spot-later.test.ts (lines 78 to 118), scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.status.map.json (the StatusBadge entries at lines 472 to 511 and 598 to 643), test/unit/redesign-status-step25.test.ts (the follow-up counts and the deviation sentence), and the browser test harness (playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/support.ts, builds.spec.ts line 99, scope-switch.spec.ts line 84, scope-switch-edges.spec.ts line 54, tokens.spec.ts, dark-spot.spec.ts lines 28 to 36, baseline.ts, baseline.json, known-violations.json) so the flag-off baseline comparison stays green and the fixture page keeps passing the specs that already read it. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules that status is shown in words beside colour and that gold #c8a94a is never text on a light ground): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 26) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy.

Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old, with package-lock.json updated by npm install; this slice needs no new package. The branch tip is a74f221 (slice 25), and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system still carries 3d80a0e (slice 24) in this container until the lead pushes, and the local main ref is 4c1a466 and does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against a74f221.

Build exactly this. Build the base components later workstreams assemble pages from.

StatusBadge.tsx:
- gains a status prop (open, soon, full, waitlist, closed, live, partner, lca) mapped to status tokens, always rendering a text label (a default label per status when no children are given)
- the live variant's dot is static, with no animation class and animation: none
- the existing tone and on props keep working unchanged for current callers
- StatusDot gains a label prop and, under newLook, renders its words visibly next to the dot, because a title attribute alone fails AC5

button.tsx gains a gold variant: gold fill, navy text, never white on gold. GOLD_BUTTON in brand.ts stays for current callers and points at the same classes.

New components:
- src/components/ui/filter-chip.tsx: a toggle with aria-pressed, an optional count, and a remove button labelled "Remove filter: <name>"
- src/components/DateBlock.tsx: weekday plus date from formatDate, inside <time dateTime>
- src/components/ScrollPanel.tsx, from K's October 8 note that long screens such as tournament setup sit in a scroll container so content stays together: a bounded, keyboard-focusable region (tabIndex 0, role region, aria-label) with overscroll-contain, a max height relative to the viewport, and an optional sticky header slot, generalising ADMIN_SCROLL

New components are used only behind flags, and no existing page changes. Applying ScrollPanel to long pages happens as WS06 and WS08 rebuild them, and REDESIGN_STATUS.md records that as a follow-up.

The manifest's risk stands: changing the defaults of the shared button primitive reaches every page, so every existing variant keeps its classes to the letter, the new styling reads tokens (src/index.css sets them for every look), and with newLook off nothing visible changes. The new components are drawn only on the fixture page (src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx, reachable in the accessibility test build only); no page file changes, and git diff against a74f221 shows none under src/pages but the fixture. StatusDot is the one existing component whose output changes with newLook on (its words appear in the /tournaments list rows); with newLook off its markup is what it is today.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): StatusBadge today. (Tones gold, emerald, red, blue and muted, on navy or light surfaces; children are optional in practice; StatusDot is colour plus a title attribute only. The light gold tone used text-[#7a5c00] (moved to a token in slice 25). Re-checked at a74f221. TONE_CLASSES (StatusBadge.tsx 26 to 41) holds the five tones on two surfaces, ten strings: the navy gold is bg-lca-gold/20 text-lca-gold (line 28, an allowlist entry for step 25's guard), the light gold is now bg-lca-gold/20 text-gold-ink-badge (line 35), and the other eight are the strings test/unit/render-smoke.test.tsx and tokens.test.ts pin. Children are not optional: the type makes both tone (BadgeTone) and children required (lines 49 and 52), and every caller passes both. The callers, counted with ripgrep over src, functions, scripts and workers: 4 StatusBadge callers in 2 files, all passing on="light" and none the navy surface, red or blue: src/pages/ScholasticPage.tsx 69 (tone={status.tone}, where TOURNAMENT_STATUS in src/areas/events/tournamentStatus.ts maps upcoming to gold, active to emerald and completed to muted, and an unknown status to upcoming) and src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx 114 (emerald), 115 (gold) and 116 (muted), each with its words in an inner span marked data-status=open, soon or closed; a fifth, test/unit/fixtures/lint/area-clean.tsx 22, is a lint fixture (tone="muted" on the default navy surface) that nothing builds. StatusDot has three states and only a title: open is a size-1.5 dot in bg-emerald-500 titled Registration open (line 80), draft is bg-lca-gold titled Opening soon (88) and anything else is bg-border titled Coming soon (95); it has no text and no aria attribute. It has one caller, src/pages/TournamentsPage.tsx 10 and 817, drawn only for an LCA event whose status is upcoming, with no label. src/pages/HomePage.tsx 128 defines its own local StatusDot (h-2 w-2, bg-ok-500, the same three titles), drawn at 237: a copy, not the shared one, so it takes none of this slice's change; record it as a follow-up for WS03.) Pulsing elements. (No animate-pulse or animate-ping in src today; keep it that way. Re-checked: 0 uses of animate-pulse, animate-ping or animate-bounce and no @keyframes anywhere in src, as the finding says. What does move is 6 animate-spin loaders (App.tsx 69, UscfSearchInput.tsx 333 and 362, ScannerPage.tsx 66, 271 and 808) and the animate-in and animate-out classes of the dialog and the select, none of them a status. The reduced-motion rule (src/index.css 759 to 771) sets animation-duration 0s !important under newLook when the browser asks for reduced motion, and the specs I read (dark-spot, scope-switch, scope-switch-edges) all run with reducedMotion reduce, so a check of AC14 run that way would pass because of the rule and prove nothing about the dot: run it with reducedMotion no-preference.) ADMIN_SCROLL. (src/lib/brand.ts exports ADMIN_SCROLL, a class string for bounded admin scroll areas; ScrollPanel generalises it. Re-checked: line 45 is 'max-h-[70vh] overflow-auto overscroll-contain', with a comment to pair it with a sticky header on tables; it has 10 uses in 9 files (ChampionsPanel.tsx 125, TournamentList.tsx 143 and 151, AuditLogPanel.tsx 253, MembersTable.tsx 179, BoardSeatsPanel.tsx 340, PostsPanel.tsx 146, AdminSupportPage.tsx 209, AdminEmailPage.tsx 609 and AdminPage.tsx 529), none of which moves in this slice. No chip, date block or scroll panel component exists in src: the only chip is TournamentsPage.tsx's local Chip (line 96, aria-pressed, navy when on), which WS04 replaces, and ui/badge.tsx is the plain pill used once, in UscfSearchInput.tsx.)

Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at a74f221. (1) The scroll area. REDESIGN_STATUS.md line 873 says step 26 adds a scroll panel and a bounded table scroll area, but the manifest gives the bounded table container, with its sticky header, to step 27 (Table's optional prop in src/components/ui/table.tsx), and the spec names neither ScrollPanel nor the table area. Build ScrollPanel only; keep line 873's heading, say in it that the table area is step 27's, and give the WS01 deviations list a step 26 sentence (ScrollPanel is not in the spec). (2) Two functions are called formatDate. DateBlock's is the one in domain/format/date.ts, re-exported by src/lib/format.ts: it returns 'Sat, Oct 24' (weekday, month, day, the year only when asked), the input string when it cannot read it and an empty string for null. src/areas/events/clearinghouse.ts line 39 has another formatDate that TournamentsPage.tsx imports, which gives 'Oct 24, 2026' with no weekday; do not use it. No file under src imports src/lib/format.ts yet. formatDate gives no machine-readable value, and zonedParts (the way to get one) is exported by domain/format/date.ts but not by the barrel domain/format/index.ts, so import it by the deep path, as domain/events/eventMode.ts does, or add the export (test/unit/format-edges.test.ts line 163 pins the folder's file list, which an export does not change; run it and domain-boundaries.test.ts all the same). The time element's dateTime must be a valid date string for a bare date, a wall-clock time and an instant alike. (3) data-status already exists, on the wrong element for a new badge. The fixture's three StatusBadge pills each wrap an inner span marked data-status (ScopeFixturePage.tsx 114 to 116), and three specs read it that way: builds.spec.ts line 99 expects exactly 3 per fixture, scope-switch.spec.ts line 84 measures each one's parentElement as the pill, and scope-switch-edges.spec.ts line 54 measures the boxes of every [data-status]. AC5's check needs data-status on every new status badge with text inside it. Either put the attribute on the new pill itself and update the three specs in step (the count, and the parent lookup for the pills that carry it), or leave the three old pills as they are and give the new ones the attribute: whichever, the fixture keeps these pins too: the Register button is the only button with that name (builds.spec.ts 97), exactly 3 th (100), the Your name field, and the buttons found by [data-slot="button"]. A new gold Button on the fixture needs another name. The page is also scanned for an en or em dash character and for the old initials of US Chess (test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts lines 460 to 490), so write any range as the file's RANGE escape does and say US Chess. (4) The guard pins StatusBadge and the fixture by line. test/unit/goldText.test.ts expects StatusBadge.tsx:28 and TournamentDetailPage.tsx:38 as the two uses it cannot place (lines 742 and 1075), lists the places a component told its ground by on is drawn, among them ScholasticPage.tsx:69 and ScopeFixturePage.tsx 114, 115 and 116 (lines 794 to 798), and plants a change in ScholasticPage.tsx (1165); fixtures/goldAllowlist.ts names TONE_CLASSES[on][tone] as the reader of StatusBadge's light gold (line 112) and the navy gold entry (line 51). So: keep TONE_CLASSES on lines 26 to 41 and put new code below it, and add fixture content after line 118 (below the Status section), or update every pin and entry in the same change; a new StatusBadge drawn on the default on="navy" on a light ground fails the guard, and any new place appears in that list. If the tone path is rewritten so its lookup is no longer TONE_CLASSES[on][tone], the allowlist's readBy and reasons change with it (follow-up line 1302). (5) Which classes the status path writes. The plain :root status tokens (index.css 252 to 267) are exactly the colours the light tones paint, held by tokens.test.ts 122 to 135: bg-status-open-tint with text-status-open is emerald-100 with emerald-800, the full pair is red-100 with red-700, the partner pair is blue-50 with blue-800 (the tone also draws a blue-200 line, which border-info-200 is on the plain :root), and the muted tone is already tokens (bg-muted text-muted-foreground). So the light tones can follow the looks without changing today's look, which is the step 24 follow-up (line 1288: take the light tones too, or keep them with a reason, and the file's keep entries and allowlist lines go). The gold tone is the catch: --status-soon is #7a5c00 and --status-soon-tint is a 20 per cent colour mix of brand gold, but the block for browsers that cannot mix colours (index.css 786 to 808) covers no status tint, while bg-lca-gold/20 carries its own fallback, so moving the gold tone (or writing a soon or LCA status badge) to bg-status-soon-tint would drop the tint for those browsers with newLook off unless the block gains a rule for it (and for --status-lca-tint, the same mix). The same two tints are translucent, so under the plain :root the soon words read 1.65:1 and the LCA words 1.44:1 on the navy surface; the status path is for light grounds and the pill on navy keeps the navy classes (measured: #7a5c00 and #1a2744 on a 20 per cent gold tint over #1a2744). The navy surface's six light-tone classes stay as step 24 kept them. (6) The pins the status path meets. contrast.test.ts lines 693 to 717 require every text-status class in a non-fixture TSX file to sit in a string with its own bg-status tint, no modifier and the same variants, and pin the list found to AgendaList.tsx 87 and TournamentDetailPage.tsx 822 (so new classes in StatusBadge.tsx join that list, each beside its tint; write each status's classes in one string of an object, which the class reader follows); the per-look test at line 111 already holds every status word to 4.5:1 on its tint. Type the props as a union, so that tone is required without a status, children are required without one, and a badge can never render empty. Under the new look --status-live and --status-lca are white or the dark ground, a pair built to be read on its own tint, so a dot for them is the words colour (bg-status-live) on that tint. The shape: the tile's tag is 24px high with a 6px radius, 12px words and a 6px gap, where today's pill is rounded-full with px-2.5 py-0.5 and text-xs; the spec (line 289) says the tile wins, the status path has no caller today, and AC8 needs the same boxes in every look, so decide the shape of the status path, keep the tone path as it is, and record both. Default labels come from the boards: Registration open, an Opens date for soon (the fixture says Opens soon), Event full (Event-Final-States), Waitlist, Closed (the fixture says Registration closed), Live, Partner event and LCA event; none of the boards names a default for every one, so choose, record and keep them in one module. (7) Where the label table can live. The linter's only-export-components rule is an error in this repository (step 24 cleared three such errors in GradeConfirm.tsx, and tournamentStatus.ts sits outside StatusBadge.tsx for this reason, per its header): StatusBadge.tsx may export components and types and nothing else but string constants, so a table of default labels, a status list or a lookup function goes in a module beside it (as APPEARANCES sits in src/lib/colorScheme.ts) or stays unexported. Measured: eslint reports nothing in StatusBadge.tsx, button.tsx, badge.tsx, brand.ts or ScopeFixturePage.tsx, and the warnings that remain in ScholasticPage.tsx (96) and TournamentsPage.tsx (402 and 413) are the fetch ones step 25 counted; no file this slice has a reason to change carries an error. Lint is 13 errors and 13 warnings at step 25; the 13 errors are in functions/ and scanner/, none in a file this slice touches. (8) The checker has never run on the fixture page. Only smoke.spec.ts (/), dark-spot.spec.ts (/, /tournaments, /membership) and the checker's own detection spec run the accessibility checker; builds.spec.ts, scope-switch*.spec.ts and tokens.spec.ts load the fixtures without it. The first run will find the muted tone: on the a11y-off build the closed badge is #737373 on #f5f5f5, 4.35:1, which the step 20 follow-up (line 1255) hands to this slice or step 32. With newLook off nothing may change, so the muted classes stay; run the contrast rule on the fixture on the a11y-on build (there the muted pill is the tile's #5b6478 on #f7f8fa) and, on a11y-off, keep that one element out with its reason written in the spec and the follow-up kept open; add nothing to known-violations.json, whose own comment forbids it. The rules the new components must satisfy are the checker's nested-interactive (FilterChip's toggle and its remove button are siblings in a group, never one button inside another), target-size at 24 by 24 pixels for the remove button (WCAG 2.2 is in the tag list), and scrollable-region-focusable for ScrollPanel. The filter chip on the tile is 32px high with a 6px radius, 13px words and a mono count in the muted ink at 11px, and selected is the soon tint with a --gold-ink border and the soon words; build it from tokens (text on a gold tint takes the badge words, never text-gold-ink, and never text-lca-gold on a light ground, or the gold guard fails the new file). (9) GOLD_BUTTON. src/lib/brand.ts lines 37 and 38 give 'bg-lca-gold font-semibold text-brand-navy hover:bg-lca-gold/90' (step 25 moved its navy from text-lca-navy). 18 files import it, 15 of them under the name GOLD, and test/unit/helpers/jsxClasses.ts line 83 reads the string with a pattern that needs a quoted literal after export const GOLD_BUTTON, which semantic-map-cascade.test.ts and semantic-map-grounds.test.ts use through goldButton(). So the literal stays in brand.ts as it is and the gold variant takes the same classes (importing the constant, or repeating it with a test that the two are equal); do not turn GOLD_BUTTON into a call. button.tsx has six variants (default, outline, secondary, ghost, destructive, link) and no gold; Button writes data-variant, and test/a11y/baseline.ts measures the first Button in main on four routes, so none of the six may change. (10) StatusDot under newLook reaches /tournaments. Its only caller passes no label, so with a default label per state the list rows on /tournaments show the words with newLook on, and dark-spot.spec.ts and dark-grounds.spec.ts read that page in dark mode on the a11y-on build: the words must reach 4.5:1 on the row's ground in every look (the row paints a club-colour tint at 5 per cent when selected). With newLook off the span, its class and its title are exactly as today. (11) The decided boards. The manifest entry names none. The spec has no ScrollPanel and plans test/a11y/scopes.spec.ts (line 369) for the static live dot where the manifest says test/a11y/components.spec.ts; the manifest's name stands, and it is the first spec to run the checker on the fixture page. The AC14 row (line 38) is this step's, and the fixture needs a live badge for it. (12) Counts to carry. The raw colour allowlist holds 43 entries and 57 uses (10 hex, 34 white veils on navy, 13 kept for whole files: StatusBadge's seven light classes and the dot 8, the print page 2 and the dots 3), and the status map's plan keeps 14 StatusBadge classes (the six navy ones among them). If the light tones and the dot move, those 8 entries leave the allowlist, the semantic-map.test.ts list (783 to 822) and dark-spot.spec.ts's LATER list (28 to 36, with dark-spot-later.test.ts) shrink to match, and the ratchet's counts become 49 uses; if any stay, each keeps its reason. The dot's open colour with the tokens is bg-ok-500, which is emerald-500 on the plain :root and the tone's words colour under the new look (HomePage's copy already uses it).

Gate before reporting: npm run lint (baseline 13 errors and 13 warnings, measured on the step 25 tree; the error total never rises from 13 and every error in a touched file is fixed; report before and after), npm run build, npm run typecheck:functions, npm run check:bundle, npm run test:all (unit 3117 in 115 files and integration 790 in 58 files before this slice; report the counts), and then PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y end to end in this container with its output quoted (both builds, the flag-off baseline compared and unchanged, the dark spot run's results; 125 passed and 30 skipped before this slice, so say how many the new spec adds on each build and which of its tests skip on the build they do not check). test/a11y/baseline.json must not be rewritten: with newLook off nothing visible changes, and a baseline difference is a defect in the slice. If an integration file fails to load as a whole on the first run, rerun that file alone once before treating it as real. Build size: step 25 recorded dist/assets CSS 122,025 bytes (one file) and JavaScript 2,568,391 bytes in 104 files, 127 files in all, and the dist folder in this container holds exactly those; report the sizes before and after. The stylesheet build reads every file in the repository for class names (index.css sets no @source; follow-up line 1273), so a test, map or record that spells out a class keeps its rule in the CSS: build the planted class names in tests when the test runs, and report the CSS growth.

Standing rules: no AI references anywhere, in code, code comments, docs or commit text; read the real file before changing it; match repo conventions; WCAG 2.2 AA; plain language ('US Chess', a weekday on every date, '7:00 PM'); status is shown in words beside colour; no em dashes in anything you write; fixtures contain nothing real; new packages exact-pinned. The recorder updates REDESIGN_STATUS.md (a step 26 block after step 25's and the Last updated line; the AC5 and AC14 rows of the acceptance table, replacing Planned with the proofs in the pattern of the T2 row, and the AC8 row only by an added sentence if the fixture's badges now draw tokens; decisions; deviations, including the ScrollPanel bullet at line 873 kept under its heading with the table area said to be step 27's; the judgement calls; each resolved verify item; the counts; and the follow-ups this step closes, by adding Done in step 26 to them and never renaming or removing one, because test/unit/redesign-status-step23.test.ts, redesign-status-step24.test.ts and redesign-status-step25.test.ts pin their headings and counts: the step 25 test counts 116 older follow-ups, exactly 8 headed step 25 and exactly 3 entries that say Done in step 25, so a follow-up this step adds is headed with (step 26) and no entry gains the words Done in step 25; the follow-ups to add include ScrollPanel's adoption on long pages as WS06 and WS08 rebuild them, HomePage's own StatusDot copy for WS03, the muted tone's 4.35:1 on today's look if it is left open, and whatever the light-tone decision leaves) and the step 26 sentence in the WS01 deviations list of docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (it deviates by adding ScrollPanel, which the spec does not name, and by adding the gold variant, the status path and the fixture's new content; keep it after step 25's sentence and write it so a test can find it), and writes test/unit/redesign-status-step26.test.ts to pin these records the way step 25's does, and drafts the commit text into <scratchpad>/slice26-commit.txt: a subject under 72 characters and plain prose, no attribution or co-author lines, no session links, no em dashes. The step records, the acceptance table and Decisions must not use the words slice, builder, scout, planner, recorder, manifest, subagent, workflow or the phrase the lead.
